_why: Which Lessons games can carry /hud.js is not derivable from the games. Twenty-six of the thirty-nine in the canonical search index already load it, Games/Glitch_Clash.html among them, so the estate's practice is that the HUD is the one permitted external script. Three games are stricter: their own verifiers forbid any <script src> at all, or extract their JavaScript by slicing to the file's last </script> and break when another one appears after it. Adding the tag to one of those is not a mechanical edit that happens to trip a check - it retracts a promise that game makes, or silently changes what its verifier reads. So the exclusions are declared here rather than left as a quiet gap.
_measured: 2026-08-10. Each entry was measured, not assumed: the verifier was run on the unmodified file (green), the script line was inserted, and the verifier was run again. Only checks that turned from green to red are recorded.
_reconciliation: The stranded figure is 13 FILES, and an earlier census made it 12. Nothing was reclassified and no file changed: the two numbers were taken from different evidence. The earlier census read the source of Trekkers_Trail_Runner (2).html, found `evLink.setAttribute('href', TREKKERS_URL)` wiring an exit to Trekkers_AQA_Evidence_L1.html, and counted it as having a way out. Driven in a browser the rendered href is still "#" - on load, and after pressing Start - with no page errors and no other control in that same setup function wired either, so the function simply never runs. The source promises an exit the runtime never delivers. Reading code is a proxy for behaviour exactly as a character count is a proxy for a byte count; the rendered attribute is the evidence. Measured across all 39: zero outward anchors, zero working scripted navigation, zero form actions, zero history.back - the partition is binary, 26 carrying the HUD and 13 not, with no third category.
_units: Counts here are FILES. 39 index entries resolve to 39 distinct files; the 13 stranded are 10 wired by this change plus the 3 excluded below. Trekkers_Trail_Runner (2).html is one file whose name contains a bracketed 2, not two files - checked by inode.
_consequence: A pupil playing one of these three has the browser Back button and the game's own navigation, and no HUD back control or chosen-homepage control. That is the status quo for all three, not a regression introduced here.

excluded.note: verify_axiomshift.js slices the shell source with html.lastIndexOf('</script>'). A later script element moves that index, so the extracted slice ends up containing a closing tag and fails node --check with SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'. The game is not at fault and neither is the tag; the extraction is anchored on a position the tag moves.
